q: You need to create 25 users in Microsoft Entra ID. Each user must sign in with the suffix @contoso.com. What must you do FIRST?
opts: Create a Microsoft 365 group named contoso.com
Add and verify the custom domain contoso.com in the tenant
Purchase Entra ID P1 licenses for all 25 users
Create a DNS zone named contoso.com in Azure DNS
exp: The UPN suffix must be a verified custom domain in the tenant (verified via a TXT record at your registrar). Groups, licenses, and Azure DNS zones do not verify domains.

q: A user account was deleted 10 days ago. What is the simplest way to get the account back with all its properties and group memberships intact?
opts: Create a new user with the same UPN
Restore the user from the Deleted users blade
Restore the tenant from a backup
Re-invite the user as a guest
exp: Within 30 days, soft-deleted users can be restored with all properties and memberships. A new user with the same UPN gets a new object ID and no memberships; tenant restore does not exist.

q: How long does Microsoft Entra ID keep a deleted user in a restorable (soft-deleted) state?
opts: 14 days
30 days
90 days
7 days
exp: When you delete a user, Microsoft Entra ID moves it to Deleted users and keeps it for 30 days. During that time you can restore it with all its properties, group memberships and licences. After 30 days it is permanently deleted and can't be recovered. 7, 14 and 90 days are not the Entra ID retention period.

q: You invite an external consultant (anna@fabrikam.com) to collaborate. Which statement is true about her account in your tenant?
opts: You must set an initial password for her
She authenticates with her own organization's credentials; her userType is Guest
She automatically gets the same default permissions as members
She can only be added to Microsoft 365 groups, not security groups
exp: With B2B collaboration, Anna signs in with her own Fabrikam account, so you never set or manage her password. Her account in your tenant has userType Guest, which gets more limited default permissions than members. Guests can be added to security groups as well as Microsoft 365 groups.

q: Which group configuration requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 license?
opts: A security group with assigned membership
A Microsoft 365 group with assigned membership
A security group with dynamic user membership
A group used for sharing a SharePoint site
exp: Dynamic membership — where Entra ID adds and removes users or devices automatically from a rule — needs a Microsoft Entra ID P1 licence. Groups with assigned (manual) membership, whether security or Microsoft 365, work on the Free tier, and sharing a SharePoint site doesn't need P1.

q: You create a dynamic user group with the rule user.department -eq "Sales". A user's department attribute is changed from "HR" to "Sales". What happens?
opts: Nothing until an admin runs a sync
The user is added to the group automatically after the rule is processed
The user receives an email invitation to join the group
The user is added only after their next sign-in
exp: Dynamic groups are re-evaluated whenever a user's attributes change. When the department becomes "Sales", the rule matches and Entra ID adds the user automatically, usually within minutes (large tenants can take longer). No admin sync, invitation or sign-in is needed.

q: Which group type can contain devices as members?
opts: Microsoft 365 group
Security group
Distribution group
Mail-enabled security group
exp: Security groups can contain users, devices, service principals and other groups, so they're used to target device settings and policies. Microsoft 365 groups and distribution groups only contain users, because they're built for collaboration and email. Mail-enabled security groups can't hold devices either.

q: A dynamic device group is being designed. Which TWO statements are true?
opts: A group can use dynamic membership for both users and devices at the same time
A group can have dynamic membership for users OR devices, not both
Dynamic membership rules can reference device properties such as deviceOSType
Device objects can only be placed in Microsoft 365 groups
exp: A dynamic group's rule targets either users or devices, never both in the same group. Device rules can use device properties such as deviceOSType, deviceOSVersion or deviceOwnership. Devices can only be members of security groups, not Microsoft 365 groups.

q: You assign licenses to the group "Sales-Users" using group-based licensing. One user shows a licensing error. The most common cause tested is:
opts: The user is a guest
The user has no usageLocation set
The user is in two groups
The group is a security group
exp: Group-based licensing fails for users without usageLocation, because many services are region-restricted. Guests can be licensed, and multiple groups merge licenses.

q: Which features require Microsoft Entra ID P2 rather than P1?
opts: Conditional Access
Dynamic groups
Privileged Identity Management (PIM) and Identity Protection
Self-service password reset with on-premises writeback
exp: Privileged Identity Management (just-in-time admin roles) and Identity Protection (risk-based sign-in and user policies) need Microsoft Entra ID P2, as do access reviews. Conditional Access, dynamic groups and SSPR with on-premises writeback only need P1.

q: Self-service password reset (SSPR) can be enabled for:
opts: All users only — no scoping possible
None, selected groups, or all users
Individual users picked one by one
Only users with the Global Administrator role
exp: In Entra ID → Password reset → Properties, SSPR can be set to None (off), Selected (one group of users) or All (every user). You can't pick individual users one by one; you put them in a group and select that group. SSPR is not limited to administrators — in fact it is aimed at ordinary users so they don't need the helpdesk.

q: Your hybrid environment syncs users from on-premises AD. Users who reset their password in the cloud must have the new password written back to on-premises AD. What do you need?
opts: Entra ID Free + Entra Connect
Entra ID P1 (or higher) and password writeback enabled in Entra Connect
Entra ID P2 only, with pass-through authentication enabled in Entra Connect
Microsoft Identity Manager
exp: Password writeback lets a password reset in the cloud be written back to on-premises AD, so the same password works on domain PCs. It needs Microsoft Entra ID P1 (or higher) and the password writeback option turned on in Entra Connect (or Cloud Sync). The Free tier can't do it, and P2 isn't required.

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement:
stmts: A guest user can be assigned an Entra ID administrative role
The userType of a user can be changed from Guest to Member after creation
A security group can be an owner of another group
Changing a user's display name changes their sign-in name
exp: Guests can be given Entra admin roles, and you can change a user's userType from Guest to Member later. Group owners must be users or service principals, not groups. And the display name is only a label: the sign-in name (UPN) doesn't change when you edit it.

q: You need to create 200 users at once in the portal. The supported method is:
opts: Upload a CSV file using the Bulk create operation in the Users blade
Upload a JSON file in the Users blade
Paste the list into the New user form
Run a PowerShell script, because the portal can create only one user at a time
exp: The Users blade has Bulk operations → Bulk create. You download a CSV template, fill in one row per user and upload it, and Entra ID creates them all. JSON isn't accepted, the New user form creates one user at a time, and PowerShell or the CLI are alternatives, not the only option.

q: Management wants to prevent standard (non-admin) users from registering applications in the tenant. Where do you configure this?
opts: Conditional Access policy
Azure RBAC on the subscription
Entra ID → Users → User settings → App registrations = No
Azure Policy assignment at tenant root = Deny app registrations
exp: "Users can register applications" is a tenant User setting. Conditional Access controls sign-in conditions; RBAC and Azure Policy govern Azure resources, not the directory.

q: Which option allows users to join their personal Windows devices to the company directory while keeping personal ownership (BYOD scenario)?
opts: Microsoft Entra join
Microsoft Entra registered
Hybrid Entra join
Domain join
exp: Microsoft Entra registered is for personal (BYOD) devices: the user keeps a personal account on the device and adds a work account, so the organisation can manage access without owning the device. Entra join is for corporate cloud-managed devices, and hybrid join or domain join is for corporate PCs in on-premises AD.

q: Which built-in role lets a user create and manage all resources in a resource group but NOT grant access to others?
opts: Owner
Contributor
User Access Administrator
Reader
exp: Contributor can create, change and delete every kind of resource in its scope, but it can't assign roles (it has no roleAssignments/write permission). Owner can also grant access to others, User Access Administrator only manages access, and Reader can only view.

q: Which built-in role can manage user access to Azure resources but cannot create or modify the resources themselves?
opts: Owner
Contributor
User Access Administrator
Security Admin
exp: User Access Administrator has full rights over Microsoft.Authorization, so it can create and remove role assignments, but it has no rights to create or change resources. Owner can do both (manage resources and access). Contributor is the opposite: it manages resources but can't grant access. Security Admin is a Defender for Cloud role, not an access-management role.

q: A role assigned at the subscription scope applies to:
opts: Only the subscription object itself
The subscription and all resource groups and resources within it
Only resource groups created after the assignment
The whole management group
exp: Azure RBAC is inherited downwards. A role assigned at a subscription applies to the subscription itself and to every resource group and resource inside it, including ones created later. It does not go upwards, so it never covers the parent management group or other subscriptions.

q: What are the three elements that make up an Azure role assignment?
opts: User, password, resource
Security principal, role definition, scope
Role definition, policy, subscription
Group, license, scope
exp: Every role assignment answers three questions: who (the security principal — a user, group, service principal or managed identity), what (the role definition, a list of allowed actions) and where (the scope — management group, subscription, resource group or resource). Policies, licences and passwords are not part of a role assignment.

q: User1 has Reader on subscription Sub1 and Contributor on resource group RG1 (inside Sub1). What can User1 do in RG1?
opts: Only read resources (Reader wins — most restrictive)
Create, modify, and delete resources
Nothing — conflicting assignments cancel out
Only actions common to both roles
exp: Azure RBAC is additive: a user's effective permissions are the combination of all their role assignments. Reader on the subscription lets User1 view everything, and Contributor on RG1 adds full management there. There's no 'most restrictive wins' — only deny assignments can take permissions away.

q: The Global Administrator of the tenant cannot see any Azure resources in a subscription. Why?
opts: Entra ID roles and Azure RBAC roles are separate
The subscription is disabled
Global Admins are blocked from Azure resources
They need an Entra ID P2 license
exp: Microsoft Entra roles (such as Global Administrator) control the directory — users, groups and settings. Azure RBAC roles (such as Owner or Reader) control Azure resources. They're separate systems, so a Global Administrator has no access to subscriptions unless they get an RBAC role or elevate their access.

q: A Global Administrator needs temporary access to manage ALL subscriptions in the tenant to fix orphaned access. The supported mechanism is:
opts: Assign Owner on each subscription one by one
Turn on "Access management for Azure resources" (elevate access)
Create a custom role with Microsoft.Authorization/* and assign it at tenant scope
Use Azure Policy to grant access
exp: A Global Administrator can turn on 'Access management for Azure resources' in the Entra properties. This elevates them to User Access Administrator at the root scope (/), so they can grant themselves access to any subscription. Turn it off again once the problem is fixed.

q: Which property of a custom RBAC role controls WHERE the role can be assigned?
opts: Actions
NotActions
AssignableScopes
DataActions
exp: AssignableScopes lists where a custom role can be assigned — specific management groups, subscriptions or resource groups. Actions and NotActions define control-plane permissions, and DataActions define data permissions, but none of these control where the role is available.

q: A custom role must allow all read operations plus restarting VMs, nothing else. Which Actions block is correct?
opts: "Actions": ["*/read", "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action"]
"Actions": ["*"], "NotActions": ["*/write", "*/delete", "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/start/action"]
"Actions": ["Microsoft.Compute/*"]
"Actions": ["*/read"], "DataActions": ["restart"]
exp: "*/read" grants every read operation, and adding "Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines/restart/action" allows exactly one extra action. "*" with NotActions "*/write" would still allow deletes and other actions, Microsoft.Compute/* allows everything on compute, and restart isn't a data action.

q: NotActions in a role definition:
opts: Creates an explicit deny that overrides every other role the user holds
Subtracts operations from the Actions of the SAME role definition only
Blocks the user tenant-wide
Is only valid in built-in roles
exp: NotActions only removes operations from that role's own Actions list. It isn't a deny: if the user has another role assignment that grants the operation, they can still do it. To block an operation no matter what other roles say, you'd need a deny assignment.

q: Which TWO role assignments allow a user to grant other users access to a resource group?
opts: Owner on the resource group
Contributor on the resource group
User Access Administrator on the resource group
Reader on the subscription
exp: To grant access, a user needs Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write. Owner and User Access Administrator both include it. Contributor explicitly excludes it, and Reader on the subscription only gives read access.

q: Which CLI command assigns the Reader role to user ali@contoso.com on resource group RG1?
opts: az role assignment create --assignee ali@contoso.com --role Reader --resource-group RG1
az ad role assignment create --user ali@contoso.com --role Reader --group RG1
az rbac grant --role Reader --rg RG1
az role definition create --role Reader
exp: az role assignment create creates a role assignment: --assignee is who, --role is what, and --resource-group (or --scope) is where. az role definition create creates a custom role rather than assigning one, and az ad role / az rbac grant are not real commands.

q: Answer Yes or No to each statement:
stmts: A role assigned at management group scope is inherited by all subscriptions under it
Deleting a user removes their role assignments' effect, but the assignment may remain as "Identity not found"
A deny assignment can be created directly by an administrator in the portal
Azure RBAC role assignments apply to Entra ID portal operations like creating users
exp: MG assignments inherit; orphaned assignments show "Identity not found"; you cannot create deny assignments directly — Azure creates them, for example from a deployment stack's deny settings; directory operations use Entra roles, not RBAC.

q: A group "Ops" has Contributor at the management group "Corp". Sub1 is in "Corp". User2 is in group "Ops". What is User2's effective role on resource group RG5 in Sub1?
opts: No access until the role is assigned directly on RG5
Contributor (inherited: MG → subscription → RG)
Reader
Owner only on RG5
exp: User2 is a member of Ops, and Ops has Contributor at the Corp management group. Role assignments to a group apply to all its members, and assignments at a management group are inherited by every subscription, resource group and resource beneath it. So User2 has Contributor on RG5 without any direct assignment.

q: A user must be able to open support tickets for a subscription and nothing more. Best-practice role?
opts: Contributor
Support Request Contributor
Owner
Billing Reader
exp: Support Request Contributor can create and manage support requests and nothing else, so it's the least-privilege choice. Contributor and Owner give far more access, and Billing Reader is for viewing invoices and billing data, not support tickets.

q: Put the steps in the correct order to grant a new vendor's engineer access to manage only VMs in RG-App:
items: Assign the "Virtual Machine Contributor" role at the RG-App scope
Invite the engineer as a guest user in Entra ID
Select the guest as the security principal
exp: First invite the engineer as a B2B guest and let them redeem the invitation, so the guest exists in your directory. Then select the guest as the principal and assign Virtual Machine Contributor at the RG-App scope. That role manages VMs only, and the scope keeps it to one resource group.

q: What is the difference between Azure Policy and Azure RBAC?
opts: They are the same service
Policy controls WHAT can be done with resources (properties/compliance); RBAC controls WHO can do actions
RBAC controls the properties that resources may have; Policy controls which identities can sign in to the tenant
Policy applies only to users; RBAC only to groups
exp: Azure Policy controls what resources may look like — allowed regions, SKUs, required tags — whoever deploys them. RBAC controls who can perform which actions. They work together: a user can have the right role and still be blocked by a policy.

q: You must prevent anyone from creating virtual machines in regions outside West Europe. What do you use?
opts: A resource lock
An Azure Policy with the "Allowed locations" definition assigned with a Deny effect
An NSG
A custom RBAC role with the West Europe region in its AssignableScopes property
exp: The built-in 'Allowed locations' policy with the Deny effect blocks any deployment outside the regions you list. Locks only stop deletes or changes, NSGs filter network traffic, and RBAC controls who can act, not where resources are created.

q: A policy with the Audit effect finds a non-compliant resource. What happens to the resource?
opts: It is deleted
It is stopped
Nothing — it is only marked non-compliant in compliance reports
It is fixed automatically at the next 24-hour compliance evaluation
exp: The Audit effect only evaluates and reports. A non-compliant resource is listed as non-compliant in the Policy compliance view and an Activity log entry is written, but nothing happens to the resource. Blocking requires Deny; fixing requires Modify or DeployIfNotExists with remediation. Policy never deletes or stops resources.

q: Which policy effect can automatically deploy a missing resource (e.g., deploy the monitoring agent if absent), and what does its remediation require?
opts: Append; requires nothing extra
DeployIfNotExists; remediation task using a managed identity
Deny; requires Owner role
Modify; remediation task using a service principal secret
exp: DeployIfNotExists checks for a related resource or setting (such as the monitoring agent) and deploys it if it's missing. Remediation tasks fix existing resources, and both run as the policy assignment's managed identity, which needs the right RBAC roles. Append and Modify change properties, and Deny blocks requests.

q: What is an Azure Policy initiative?
opts: A policy definition that cannot be changed once it is assigned
A group of policy definitions assigned together as one unit
A policy assigned at tenant root
A deny assignment
exp: An initiative (also called a policy set) groups several policy definitions so you can assign them, parameterise them and track their compliance as one unit — for example a regulatory standard with dozens of controls. It is still changeable, can be assigned at any scope, and has nothing to do with deny assignments.

q: A policy denying public IP creation is assigned at the subscription. One resource group RG-Lab must be exempt. The BEST approach is:
opts: Move RG-Lab to another tenant
Add RG-Lab as an exclusion (or create a policy exemption) on the assignment
Delete the policy
Assign a second policy at RG-Lab that allows public IPs, since the closest scope wins
exp: Policy assignments have exclusions (the scope isn't evaluated) and exemptions (evaluated but marked Exempt, optionally with an expiry), so exclude RG-Lab or create an exemption for it. A second 'allow' policy can't override a deny, because all policies apply together. Moving tenants or deleting the policy is overkill.

q: Existing non-compliant resources that were created BEFORE a Deny policy was assigned are:
opts: Deleted automatically
Left running but reported as non-compliant
Stopped automatically
Moved to a quarantine resource group
exp: A Deny policy only blocks create and update requests made after the assignment. Resources that already existed are not deleted, stopped or moved; the next compliance scan simply marks them as non-compliant so you can fix them. To change existing resources automatically you'd need a Modify or DeployIfNotExists policy with a remediation task.

q: Which lock type allows users to read and modify a resource but prevents deletion?
opts: ReadOnly
CanNotDelete
NoDelete
Protect
exp: A CanNotDelete lock (shown as Delete in the portal) lets authorised users read and change a resource but blocks deleting it. A ReadOnly lock is stricter: it blocks deletes and all changes. NoDelete and Protect are not Azure lock types.

q: A ReadOnly lock is applied to a storage account. Which unexpected side effect is commonly tested?
opts: Blobs can no longer be read by users who have the Storage Blob Data Reader role
Operations like listing storage account keys fail, because list keys is a POST action
The account is deleted after 30 days
The firewall is disabled
exp: A ReadOnly lock only allows GET (read) requests on the control plane. Listing storage account keys is a POST operation (listKeys), so it fails — which also breaks portal tools that use account keys to browse data. Reading blobs with existing credentials still works, and nothing is deleted or disabled.

q: A CanNotDelete lock is applied at the resource group level. Which statement is true?
opts: Only the resource group object is protected; resources inside can be deleted
All resources within the resource group inherit the lock and cannot be deleted
The lock expires after 90 days
Owners can delete resources despite the lock without removing it
exp: Locks are inherited: a CanNotDelete lock on a resource group protects the group and every resource in it, including resources added later. Locks don't expire. Even an Owner has to remove the lock before deleting anything.

q: Which roles can create or delete management locks?
opts: Any Contributor
Owner and User Access Administrator
Reader
Only Global Administrator
exp: Creating or deleting locks needs Microsoft.Authorization/locks/* permissions. Owner and User Access Administrator have them. Contributor and Reader don't, and Global Administrator is an Entra role with no Azure access by default.

q: Resource group RG1 has the tag env=prod. VM1 is created inside RG1. What tag does VM1 have?
opts: env=prod, inherited automatically
No tags — tags are not inherited by default
env=prod but read-only
A system tag linking it to RG1
exp: Tags aren't inherited by default. Resources in a resource group don't get its tags automatically, so VM1 has no tags. To copy tags down automatically, use the built-in 'Inherit a tag from the resource group' policy.

q: You must ensure every NEW resource gets the tag costcenter copied from its resource group automatically. What do you use?
opts: A resource lock
The built-in Azure Policy "Inherit a tag from the resource group" with the Modify effect
The built-in Azure Policy "Require a tag on resources" with the Audit effect enabled
Azure Advisor
exp: The built-in policy 'Inherit a tag from the resource group if missing' (or 'Inherit a tag from the resource group') uses the Modify effect to add the tag to new or updated resources. A remediation task applies it to existing resources. Locks, templates and Advisor don't copy tags.

q: You move a VM from RG1 to RG2 within the same subscription. Which statement is true?
opts: The VM's region changes to RG2's region
The VM keeps its region
The VM restarts during the move
Moving VMs between resource groups is not supported
exp: Moving a resource between resource groups only changes its metadata. The VM keeps its region and keeps running without a restart. While the move runs, both resource groups are locked against create, update and delete operations.

q: How many levels of depth does a management group hierarchy support (excluding the root management group and subscriptions)?
opts: Unlimited
exp: A management group tree can be up to six levels deep. The tenant root management group and the subscription level don't count towards those six. This is a fixed platform limit, so 'unlimited' is wrong.

q: You assign a policy at the "Corp" management group and an RBAC Reader role at the root management group to user Bob. Which statement applies to new subscription Sub9 placed under "Corp"?
opts: Neither applies until manually linked
Both are inherited: Sub9 gets the policy, Bob can read Sub9's resources
Only RBAC is inherited: Bob can read Sub9, but the policy must be assigned again
Only policy inherits, RBAC never inherits
exp: Both RBAC role assignments and policy assignments are inherited down the hierarchy. Bob's Reader role at the root applies to every subscription, and the policy on Corp applies to everything under Corp. So Sub9 gets both automatically.

q: A monthly budget of $500 with an alert at 80% is configured on a subscription. Spending reaches $500. What happens to the running resources?
opts: All resources are deallocated automatically
Nothing — budgets alert but never stop resources by themselves
The subscription is cancelled
New deployments are blocked until the next billing period starts
exp: Budgets only send notifications (email or action groups) when thresholds are reached. They never stop or deallocate resources by themselves, block deployments or cancel the subscription. To stop resources automatically, attach an action group that runs automation such as a runbook or Logic App.

ctx: Contoso has management group MG-Prod containing Sub1. RG-Fin in Sub1 has a CanNotDelete lock. A policy at MG-Prod denies creating resources outside West Europe. User1 has Contributor on Sub1.
q: Answer Yes or No:
stmts: User1 can create a storage account in East US in RG-Fin
User1 can delete a VM inside RG-Fin
User1 can create a VM in West Europe in RG-Fin
User1 can remove the lock on RG-Fin
exp: The policy denies non-West-Europe creates; the inherited CanNotDelete lock blocks deletes; Contributor + compliant region allows the create; Contributor lacks Microsoft.Authorization/locks permissions.
